The park-boundary vegetation to the right has ended — fully in public street space now. A residential building with a decorative rendered facade in the mid-distance. The dense northern-boundary vegetation (elder, birch, mixed shrubs in full summer leaf) fills the right of the frame, opaque and immediate. To the left, the urban street: road surface, building facades, tram catenary wires, ordinary suburban infrastructure of Hirschwiesenstrasse. The complete transition from park-world to city-world is captured in a single frame — the very essence of Irchelpark's design, a wild-seeming landscape pressed right up against, and concealing, the dense infrastructure of the city. The walk is complete: ~12 min 44 s circling the lower park from the northern Hirschwiesenstrasse entrance, taking in the lookout mound, the Finnenbahn running track, the Allmendsee/Irchelweiher and its wooden boardwalk and jetties, the daylighted streams and ponds, the granite Riviera staircase, the University of Zürich Irchel campus with Cinelli's "Sonnennadeln," the Allmendwiese meadows and boulder play areas, the barbecue/picnic spots, and finally the tram-tunnel infrastructure at the park's northern seam. ================================================================================ APPENDIX A — TYPES OF PATHS / SURFACES IDENTIFIED 1. Perimeter asphalt path: smooth fine grey bitumen, used as the main pedestrian access and the outer ring; appears at the entrance/exit and along the road-side edge. 2. Finnenbahn (soft running track): the signature pale, reddish-brown crushed-bark-and-aggregate resilient surface, springy and matte, forming the ~2.5 km jogging loop; explicitly designed to spare runners' joints. 3. Compacted fine gravel walking paths: the interior network linking meadows, lake and water features. 4. Cobblestone / sett paving: at the campus forecourt and Riviera staircase transition squares. 5. Granite/sandstone stepped terrace ("Riviera"): the wide, shallow, grass-jointed steps bridging the lower park and campus over the buried roads. 6. Wooden boardwalks and rustic timber jetties (Holzstege): the lake-edge deck and post-and-beam observation structures. 7. Stepping stones and flat granite slabs: at stream crossings and lake margins, doubling as informal seating/viewing platforms. APPENDIX B — HOW THE SPACE IS USED (observed in video) - Running/jogging on the Finnenbahn (a runner at ~0:50–1:14). - Dog-walking on the perimeter ring (couple with Golden Retriever, ~0:20). - Family outings with young children (multiple groups, e.g. ~1:54, ~8:10). - Sitting/sunbathing on the Riviera steps and lake boardwalk (groups visible throughout the staircase, ~3:44, ~4:14–4:34). - Picnicking/lounging on the open meadows; barbecue/fire-pit use near the lake. - Children's informal play on the granite boulders and at the stream edges. - Walking/strolling and nature observation along the water features (Naturlehrpfad nature-trail boards). - The space functions simultaneously as a university campus park (students crossing to/from the Irchel campus), a neighbourhood recreation ground, and an urban nature reserve. APPENDIX C — FLORA / FAUNA NOTES (visual + research) Visually identifiable woody species: pedunculate oak (Quercus robur), silver birch (Betula pendula), hornbeam (Carpinus betulus), large-leaved linden (Tilia platyphyllos), sycamore maple (Acer pseudoplatanus), Scots pine (Pinus sylvestris), elder (Sambucus nigra, in flower), hazel (Corylus avellana), willows (Salix spp., incl. weeping/white/crack willow), alder (Alnus glutinosa), dog-rose (Rosa canina), rowan (Sorbus aucuparia), bramble (Rubus fruticosus), butterfly-bush (Buddleja davidii). Marginal/aquatic: common reed (Phragmites australis), reed canary-grass (Phalaris arundinacea), water mint (Mentha aquatica), sedges (Carex spp.), duckweed (Lemna minor); meadow plants incl. rosebay willowherb (Epilobium angustifolium), white clover, plantain. Documented fauna (UZH 2024): 92 bird species (incl. mallard, grey heron, kingfisher, cormorant, corvids), 12 mammals, 5 amphibians, 4 reptiles, 11 fish; ~500 plant species and 86 mosses overall. APPENDIX D — EVENTS & HERITAGE - The temporary barriers and the pale wood-chip/sawdust line on the Finnenbahn are residue from a spring city RELAY RACE (Stadtlauf-type event) held the weekend before recording; the eco-friendly biodegradable course-marking fits the park's environmental ethos. - The park is under heritage protection (Denkmalschutz) as a landmark of the Swiss Naturgarten movement and a "Park-Ikone." - Winning competition project (1979): "Terra," by Atelier Stern + Partner with Eduard Neuenschwander. Park built 1982–1986, inaugurated 1986. - Public artworks: "Sonnennadeln" (Albert Cinelli), "Sturm" (Wolfgang Häckel), "Raumwandler" (Florin Granwehr), "Bruder Sonne, Schwester Mond" (Roland Hotz). The Anthropologisches Museum is on campus.
